pageCache.text:
Our Academy
Strong female leadership combined with nurture and academic achievement are at the heart of Atlantic Academy Portland’s transformation into one of Dorset’s top schools. This all-through school has been on an incredible journey that reflects the hard work, passion and determination shown by Leaders to turn their school into a success. The efforts of the leadership team and those of all staff at the school were recognised when Ofsted praised the‘’remarkable turnaround’’ of the school and gave it a ‘Good’ rating in its first inspection since being taken over. The school, for pupils aged 4 to 16, was taken over by Aspirations Academies Trust and re- named Atlantic Academy Portland in 2017. The ‘Good’ rating applies to the whole school and in all areas from the quality of the education through to leadership and management and early years provision.

Values and Ethos
Atlantic Academy – Self worth, Engagement and Purpose
Vision
By providing an exceptional all-through education, we will transform the lives of every student – nurturing their self-worth, inspiring engagement in learning, and guiding them to discover a strong sense of purpose.
Mission
We provide a safe, inclusive, and ambitious learning environment where high expectations, strong relationships, and excellent teaching enable every student to thrive academically, socially, and personally.
Our Core Principals are underpinned by the Aspirations Trusts values and ethos. We are developing an educational framework that delivers high aspirations, high levels of academic performance and the development of the skills required for success in the 21st century workplace: No limits: Education for success in the 21st century
The core principles of this framework are:
Self-worth, Engagement, Purpose
Innovation and Enterprise
Challenge and Engagement
With big dreams and hard work anything is possible

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Our Academy
Welcome from the Principal
I am honoured to lead the team at Atlantic Academy, a unique, all-through education, for the students of Portland, working to transform their lives; inspiring them to have the confidence, character and commitment to realise their full potential.
Our goal is to deliver a rigorous, engaging curriculum, to improve outcomes for all our students and provide opportunities for cultural enrichment. We want all our students to live happy, healthy and productive lives.
Our school’s unique nature and small size ensures we know our children well and enable them to realise their ambitions, helping them to strive to achieve their very best.
We are an integral part of the Portland community. Portland and Portland’s future matter to us and we will equip the children in our care with the skills, attitudes, academic qualifications and imagination needed for the complex and changing world ahead.
In choosing Atlantic Academy Portland for your child, you will be joining an exceptional team.
We are delighted to welcome you and your child to the Academy.
Our website aims to give you a flavour of life at the Academy but the best way to find out what we’re about is to arrange a visit. We are always happy to give tours and discuss the needs of your child with you on an individual basis, so please make an appointment via the office and we look forward to meeting you personally.

pageCache.text:
Our Universal Offer
Our Universal Offer
Inclusive teaching. Positive relationships. Opportunities for every pupil.
At Atlantic Academy, we believe that every child and young person should have access to high-quality teaching, a supportive learning environment and the opportunity to succeed.
Our Universal Offer is the foundation of inclusion across the academy, from Reception through to Year 11. It describes the approaches and adjustments that form part of everyday teaching and school life, helping pupils develop their knowledge, confidence, independence and sense of belonging.
We recognise that pupils learn in different ways and may experience different barriers to learning and participation. Our teachers and support staff work together to understand these needs and respond through inclusive classroom practice.
High expectations remain at the heart of our approach. We aim to make learning accessible and provide appropriate support while maintaining an ambitious curriculum for all.
What Does Our Universal Offer Look Like?
Our Universal Offer encompasses four broad areas of need. Many of the approaches described below benefit all pupils, while particular strategies may be especially helpful for those experiencing additional difficulties.
Cognition and Learning
Helping pupils understand, remember and apply their learning.
We recognise that pupils develop knowledge and skills at different rates. Our teaching approaches help pupils access new learning, build upon what they already know and become increasingly independent.
Our aim is to help pupils experience success, develop confidence and build the knowledge and skills needed for future learning.
Communication and Interaction
Creating classrooms where pupils can understand, communicate and participate confidently.
Effective communication is central to learning and positive relationships. We recognise that pupils may need different levels of support to understand instructions, express their ideas and interact with others.
Our approaches include:
These approaches help pupils feel confident in communicating their ideas, understanding expectations and participating in learning.
Modelling spoken language and explaining unfamiliar vocabulary.
Social, Emotional and Mental Health
Supporting wellbeing, positive relationships and a strong sense of belonging.
We recognise that pupils learn best when they feel safe, respected and supported.
Our Universal Offer promotes emotional wellbeing and positive relationships through:
We want every pupil to feel that they are a valued member of the Atlantic community and that support is available when they need it.
Warm, respectful relationships between pupils and staff.
Positive approaches to behaviour and emotional regulation.
Communication and partnership with parents and carers.
Sensory and/or Physical Needs
Making learning environments accessible, comfortable and supportive.
We aim to ensure that pupils can access their learning and participate safely and confidently in school life.
Our Universal Offer includes:
We recognise that small adjustments can make a significant difference to a pupil’s comfort, confidence and participation.
Thoughtful classroom organisation and seating arrangements.
Understanding Individual Needs
Although our Universal Offer is available to all pupils, we recognise that some children and young people benefit from particular strategies being used consistently.
Where a pupil has identified additional needs or barriers to learning, helpful classroom approaches and reasonable adjustments may be recorded in an individual Learning Plan.
Learning Plans help staff understand a pupil’s strengths, needs and the approaches that support them most effectively.
Having a Learning Plan does not automatically mean that a pupil requires specialist intervention or support outside the classroom.
When Additional Support Is Needed
For some pupils, inclusive classroom practice may need to be supplemented by more specific or intensive support.
Our graduated approach allows us to identify additional needs, plan appropriate provision and review its impact.
Families can explore the next levels of our Inclusion and SEND Offer:
Our Targeted Offer — Additional planned support for identified needs.
Our Targeted Plus Offer — Highly personalised and coordinated support.
These levels are flexible, and pupils may benefit from different types of support at the same time.
Working Together
We value the knowledge and experience that parents and carers bring to understanding their children.
If you have concerns about your child’s learning, communication, wellbeing or participation in school life, we encourage you to contact the academy.
Further information about raising concerns, identifying additional needs and reviewing support is available on our Supporting Your Child page.
Everyday inclusion. High-quality teaching. Success for every pupil.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years Foundation Stage - Reception - Atlantic Academy
pageCache.text:
Early Years Foundation Stage – Reception
Our Reception curriculum is designed to enable all pupils to develop their independent learning skills, enabling them to grow into happy, confident students who are ready to start the next stage of their learning journey in Key Stage 1.
By the end of the year, our aim is that our students are confident in the following areas;
Read and write full sentences;
Work confidently with numbers up to 20;
Form friendships and work as a team
Manage their own feelings and behaviour;
Assessment
We assess children’s development throughout Reception with daily observations of their interactions and play, as well as through more structured learning opportunities, such as reading or writing in small groups with a teacher. Assessments are carried out using an online journal named ‘Tapestry’, this creates a seamless dialogue between the Academy and parents/careers.
We map each child’s progress against Development Matters statements, which allows us to identify areas of strength, as well as the key next steps for each child.
Curriculum
As with all areas of our Primary phase curriculum, all of our learning in Reception is linked to a central topic, such as All About Me or Seasides. Our topic mapping has been specially designed to support the needs of the students at Atlantic in addition to supporting the 7 areas of learning the Early Years curriculum focuses on.
During a ‘typical’ Academy day in Reception we will start the day with Phonics and Talk 4 Writing. We then study Maths before attending Family Dining at Lunch time. After Lunch we have our Independent Learning time – where we explore the tasks and activities in the Reception Learning space.We aim to ensure all students in Reception are read with every single day.
Curriculum Enrichment
We have the opportunity to go on a number of trips and experiences through the Year such as a trip to Kingston Maurward, our local library and a visit to our Local Farm.
Reception takes part in ‘Beach School’ throughout the academic year. Each week we take the children down to a variety of beaches in our local area to explore our natural environment and learn. Beach school is a great way to encourage children to not only work as part of a team, but to also explore and think independently whilst being guided in a safely assessed session.
Home Learning
In Reception it is essential that students read every day to support their development in early reading. 10 minutes reading a day to an adult will support the academic work your child completed in class. All students are expected to bring their book bag into school every day with a signed reading log.
Communication with parents
We know that by working in Partnership with parents and carers will ensure the students at our school have the very best start to their educational career.
We ensure all staff are available every morning at drop off and pick up, and a termly newsletter and digital letters are shared with details about events and/or activities. We report students’ progress 2 times a year with a data report demonstrating progress and twice a year we hold a consultation meeting discussing your child’s progress and next steps. Our online Learning journal Tapestry will ensure that communication and daily activities are communicated easily and will ensure that any developments at home can be shared with your child’s class teacher.

Atlantic PTA
Welcome to the PTA
The PTA is made up of parents, teachers and any other volunteer who would like to get involved with the academy fundraising.
The purpose of the PTA is to raise funds which enable the children to engage in extra curricular activities, special purchases not usually provided by the academy and to put on a variety of events for the pupils, parents and the local community.
In the past, the monies raised have been used for visits to the school by various organisations, including a mobile planetarium and a ‘Bugfest’, to subsidise trips and transport for competitions like the Global Rock dance challenge.
This year we have decided to focus mainly on fundraising to improve the outside areas for all children. In the spring we held an adult Race Night which raised £1400. This has been ‘ring fenced’ specifically for us to make match funding applications.
We have a school lottery set up by one of our volunteers last year and this has the potential to bring in good revenue. Due to the name change the link to this is unavailable at this time but will be updated here as soon as possible so please keep checking back.
Another way you can help is by signing up to the Easyfundraising app. This app is totally free to use. If you do online shopping there are 100’s of well known retailers signed up to it, all you do is shop via the app and every single purchase you make generates funds for our organisation at no extra cost to yourself. It doesn’t matter if you already use this for a different cause as you can switch between causes as you wish. For more information please follow this link:
https://www.easyfundraising.org.uk/causes/atlanticacademy
We always need volunteers, whether it’s helping to organise events, helping at events or just coming up with new ideas. We aim to hold termly meetings, sometimes more frequent if our time allows, but we realise it is hard for people to attend meetings (it’s also hard to organise a convenient time for everybody), so please don’t feel that if you can’t attend, that you won’t be able to help in any way.

Inclusion
Our Approach to Inclusion
At Atlantic Academy, we believe that every child and young person deserves to feel valued, included and supported to succeed.
We believe that inclusion is not a place or a label — it is a culture. We celebrate what works, learn from challenges, and adapt with integrity.
Our commitment is to ensure that every student, regardless of need or background, experiences a high-quality education that builds confidence, independence, and a sense of pride in their learning.
As an all-through academy, from Reception to Year 11, we recognise that our pupils bring different strengths, experiences and needs to school. Our responsibility is to understand these differences, remove barriers to learning and participation, and ensure that every pupil has the opportunity to thrive.
Our approach is rooted in the Aspirations Academies Trust’s three guiding principles: Self-Worth, Engagement and Purpose. We want every pupil to develop confidence in themselves, feel connected to their school community and experience success throughout their education.
How can we help you?
I am worried about my child
What support is available?
Learning plans and EHCPS
SEND and Accessibility information
Inclusion Is Everyone’s Responsibility
Inclusion is not something that happens separately from everyday school life. It is central to our teaching, curriculum, relationships and expectations.
We believe that high-quality teaching is the foundation of inclusive education. Our teachers and support staff work together to understand pupils’ needs, adapt approaches where appropriate and maintain high aspirations for everyone.
Inclusion does not mean lowering expectations. It means providing the right support and opportunities so that every pupil can work towards achieving them.
Our Seven Principles of Inclusion
Our approach is guided by seven principles that help us create an ambitious, welcoming and accessible school environment.
1. Ambition for Every Pupil
We maintain high expectations for all pupils. Our leaders and staff share responsibility for ensuring that inclusion is considered in curriculum planning, teaching and wider school life.
2. Early Identification and Support
We work to recognise barriers to learning and participation early, using assessment, observation and communication with families to identify appropriate, evidence-informed support.
3. Inclusive Teaching and Curriculum
We use clear explanations, modelling, scaffolding and regular checks for understanding to help pupils access an ambitious curriculum, develop independence and make progress.
4. Opportunities for Everyone
We want pupils to benefit from the full experience of school life, including sport, the arts, educational visits, enrichment activities and our house system. We seek to remove barriers that might limit participation.
5. Belonging, Respect and Wellbeing
We promote positive relationships, a safe and respectful environment, and a strong sense of belonging. Our pastoral and inclusion teams support pupils’ wellbeing, attendance and engagement.
6. Working Together
We value strong partnerships with pupils, parents, carers and external professionals. By sharing information and listening to different perspectives, we can make better decisions about support.
7. Accessible Learning Environments
We consider the physical, sensory and communication needs of our pupils and make appropriate adjustments to help them participate confidently and safely in learning and school life.
The Right Support at the Right Time
We recognise that pupils may need different types of support at different stages of their education.
Our Inclusion and SEND Offer is organised around three flexible levels:
Universal Support — Inclusive teaching, positive relationships and appropriate adjustments that form part of everyday school life.
Targeted Support — Additional, planned interventions and adjustments for pupils who need more specific support.
Targeted Plus Support — Highly personalised, coordinated or specialist support for pupils with more complex or persistent needs.
These are not fixed categories. Pupils may receive different types of support at the same time, depending on their individual needs. A formal diagnosis or Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) is not required to access appropriate additional support.
Explore our SEND & Additional Needs Offer to find out more.

SEND & Additional Needs
SEND & Additional Needs
At Atlantic Academy, we are committed to ensuring that children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) receive the support they need to learn, participate and thrive.
Our approach is built upon high-quality inclusive teaching, positive relationships and close partnership with pupils and their families.
From Reception through to Year 11, we recognise that every pupil has their own strengths, experiences and needs. We work to identify barriers to learning, provide appropriate support and help pupils develop the confidence and independence to succeed.
At Atlantic Academy we have two, phase specific SENDCos, one who oversees primary and one for secondary. They are supported by a wider team of dedicated colleagues.
Miss Ramsey (Primary SENDCo)
Mrs Delage-Townsend (Secondary SENDCo)
Mr Andrew Clark (Assistant Principal, Inclusion)
Contact Our Inclusion Team
Our Inclusion and SEND Offer
We recognise that pupils may need different types of support at different times.
Our Inclusion and SEND Offer describes the provision available across the academy, from everyday inclusive classroom practice to more individualised and specialist support.
It is organised into three flexible levels.
Universal — Support for All Pupils
Our Universal Offer is the foundation of inclusion at Atlantic Academy.
It includes high-quality inclusive teaching, accessible learning environments, positive relationships and appropriate reasonable adjustments.
Teachers adapt their approaches to help pupils access learning, develop independence and participate fully in school life.
Explore Our Universal Offer
Targeted — Additional Support for Identified Needs
Some pupils benefit from additional support to address specific barriers to learning, communication, emotional wellbeing or participation.
Our Targeted Offer includes planned interventions, adjustments and additional support, usually delivered alongside a pupil’s normal classroom experience.
Support may be provided individually or in small groups, with clear intended outcomes and regular reviews.
Explore Our Targeted Offer
Targeted Plus — Highly Personalised Support
A smaller number of pupils may require more intensive, individualised or specialist provision because their needs are complex, significant or persistent.
Our Targeted Plus Offer involves carefully planned and coordinated support, which may include specialist professionals working alongside academy staff, pupils and their families.
The focus remains on learning, wellbeing, independence and participation in mainstream school life.
Explore Our Targeted Plus Offer
Understanding the Four Broad Areas of Need
Our provision is informed by the four broad areas of special educational need identified in the SEND Code of Practice.
A pupil may have needs across more than one area. Our approach considers the individual rather than relying on a single category or label.
Support That Responds to Individual Needs
Our three levels of support are not fixed categories or a sequence that every pupil must follow.
A pupil may receive different types of support at the same time, and their provision may change as their needs develop.
Reasonable adjustments can be made at any level. Pupils do not need a formal diagnosis or an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) to receive appropriate additional support.
Where individual needs are identified, staff may use a Learning Plan to record helpful strategies and promote consistent support across lessons.
We regularly consider the impact of support and make changes where appropriate, working in partnership with pupils, families and relevant professionals.
Working Together to Support Your Child
Parents and carers play an important role in helping us understand their child’s strengths, experiences and needs.
If you have concerns about your child’s learning, development or wellbeing, we encourage you to contact the academy so that we can discuss those concerns and consider appropriate next steps.
You can find further information about how we identify needs, plan and review support, and work with families on our Supporting Your Child page.
For more detailed information about our SEND provision, please visit our SEND Information & Accessibility page.
High expectations. The right support. Opportunities for all.

Our Targeted Offer
Our Targeted Offer
Recognising individual needs. Providing additional support. Building confidence and independence.
At Atlantic Academy, we recognise that some children and young people benefit from additional support to overcome particular barriers to learning, communication, emotional wellbeing or participation in school life.
Our Targeted Offer builds upon the high-quality teaching and inclusive approaches provided through our Universal Offer. It provides planned interventions, adjustments and additional support for pupils who need something more specific to help them succeed.
Targeted support may be delivered individually or in small groups, usually alongside a pupil’s normal classroom experience.
The support provided is based on identified needs, with clear intended outcomes and regular opportunities to review progress.
What Does Our Targeted Offer Look Like?
Our Targeted Offer addresses the four broad areas of special educational need. The examples below illustrate some of the approaches and interventions that may be used at Atlantic Academy.
Support is selected according to individual needs, and not every intervention will be appropriate or available for every pupil.
Cognition and Learning
Developing essential skills and overcoming barriers to learning.
Some pupils benefit from additional teaching, structured interventions or personalised resources to help them develop their knowledge, understanding and independence.
Our Targeted Offer may include:
These approaches aim to strengthen pupils’ foundational knowledge and skills, build confidence and help them participate more independently in their learning.
Additional teacher-led mathematics support.
Communication and Interaction
Supporting understanding, communication and positive social interaction.
Some pupils require additional strategies to understand information, express themselves, manage changes to routines or develop confidence in communicating with others.
Our Targeted Offer may include:
Our aim is to help pupils communicate confidently, understand expectations and develop the skills needed to participate positively in classroom and wider school life.
Interventions to develop communication and social skills.
Pre-teaching vocabulary and introducing communication strategies.
Personalised seating, movement and attention strategies.
Social, Emotional and Mental Health
Building emotional wellbeing, positive relationships and engagement with school.
We recognise that some pupils need additional support to manage emotions, develop confidence, maintain positive relationships or engage consistently with their education.
Our Targeted Offer may include:
These approaches aim to help pupils develop emotional understanding, build positive relationships and feel increasingly confident and secure in school.
Regular check-ins with an identified, trusted adult.
Individual mentoring and pastoral support.
Planned support to improve attendance and engagement.
Sensory and/or Physical Needs
Making appropriate adjustments to support comfort, access and participation.
Some pupils benefit from additional adjustments to their environment, routines or resources to help them access learning and participate comfortably in school life.
Our Targeted Offer may include:
Our aim is to reduce barriers, promote independence and help pupils participate as fully as possible in learning and wider school activities.
Adapted workstations, seating arrangements or classroom organisation.
Adapted timetables or transition arrangements where appropriate.
Planning and Reviewing Support
Targeted support is planned in response to an identified need rather than a particular diagnosis or label.
When considering additional provision, staff draw upon information from teachers, assessments, observations and discussions with pupils and their families.
Where appropriate, support may be recorded in an individual Learning Plan, helping staff understand the pupil’s strengths, needs, strategies and intended outcomes.
We regularly review the impact of interventions and adjustments, considering whether support should continue, change or be reduced as pupils develop their skills and independence.
Our approach is flexible, recognising that pupils’ needs may change over time.
Working Alongside Everyday Teaching
Targeted support is intended to complement, rather than replace, high-quality classroom teaching.
Teachers remain responsible for the learning and progress of the pupils they teach, working alongside the Inclusion Team, pastoral staff and other professionals where appropriate.
We aim to ensure that additional support helps pupils develop the knowledge, skills and confidence needed to participate successfully in their usual lessons and wider school life.
When More Personalised Support Is Needed
For a smaller number of pupils, additional needs may be more complex, significant or persistent and require a more individualised or coordinated approach.
Our Targeted Plus Offer explains how we may work with families and specialist professionals to plan more intensive support.
You can also explore:
Our Universal Offer — The inclusive teaching approaches and adjustments that support all pupils.
Supporting Your Child — How we identify needs, plan and review provision, and work in partnership with families.
Our Targeted Plus Offer — Highly personalised and coordinated support for pupils with more complex or persistent needs.
Additional support. Clear goals. Growing independence.

pageCache.text:
Our Targeted Plus Offer
Our Targeted Plus Offer
Personalised support. Working together. Helping every pupil thrive.
At Atlantic Academy, we recognise that some children and young people experience more complex, significant or persistent needs that require a highly personalised approach to learning and participation in school life.
Our Targeted Plus Offer builds upon the inclusive teaching and additional support provided through our Universal and Targeted Offers.
For a smaller number of pupils, this may involve carefully coordinated support, specialist advice, individualised learning programmes or additional arrangements to help them access their education.
Our aim is to ensure that every pupil continues to experience high expectations, a sense of belonging and opportunities to develop confidence, independence and success.
What Does Our Targeted Plus Offer Look Like?
Targeted Plus provision is planned around the individual pupil and their identified needs.
Support may involve teachers, the Inclusion Team, pastoral staff, specialist professionals, parents and carers, and the pupil themselves.
The examples below illustrate the types of personalised provision that may be considered. Support is determined by individual circumstances, professional advice and the resources and services available.
Cognition and Learning
Providing personalised approaches to support learning and independence.
Some pupils require more individualised teaching approaches or specialist support to help them access the curriculum and develop essential knowledge and skills.
Our Targeted Plus Offer may include:
Our focus is on helping pupils overcome barriers to learning while developing the knowledge, confidence and independence needed to participate successfully in their education.
Coordinated support linked to individual learning outcomes.
Communication and Interaction
Developing communication, understanding and confidence in social situations.
Some pupils benefit from specialist advice or highly personalised strategies to support communication, interaction and participation in school life.
Our Targeted Plus Offer may include:
These approaches aim to help pupils communicate effectively, build positive relationships and participate with increasing confidence and independence.
Individual communication plans informed by specialist recommendations.
Enhanced visual and communication systems.
Individual sensory and communication profiles.
Involvement of specialist teachers or outreach services.
Social, Emotional and Mental Health
Providing coordinated support for wellbeing, engagement and participation.
We recognise that some pupils experience significant or persistent social, emotional or mental health needs that affect their ability to engage with learning or attend school consistently.
For these pupils, a more individualised and coordinated approach may be required, involving academy staff, families and, where appropriate, external professionals.
Our Targeted Plus Offer may include:
Our priority is to help pupils feel safe, supported and connected to their education, while working towards sustained engagement, participation and successful learning.
Where individual arrangements are required, these are carefully planned and reviewed, with a clear focus on the pupil’s educational needs and longer-term outcomes.
Individual emotional regulation and support plans.
Coordinated support through The Harbour, where appropriate.
Sensory and/or Physical Needs
Making personalised adjustments to enable access, safety and participation.
Some pupils require specialist assessment, equipment or individual arrangements to help them access learning and the wider school environment.
Our Targeted Plus Offer may include:
We aim to ensure that pupils can participate safely, comfortably and confidently in their learning and wider school experiences.
Specialist sensory assessments and recommendations.
Occupational Therapy referrals and advice.
Highly personalised adaptations to the learning environment.
Specialist equipment or assistive technology.
Planning and Coordinating Support
Targeted Plus provision is carefully planned and reviewed to ensure that it remains appropriate to each pupil’s needs.
Where additional support is required, we work with pupils, parents and carers, teaching staff and relevant professionals to identify priorities and agree appropriate strategies.
Support may be recorded through an individual Learning Plan or other relevant support arrangements, helping staff understand the pupil’s strengths, needs and intended outcomes.
We use a graduated approach of Assess, Plan, Do, Review, considering the impact of provision and making adjustments as needs develop.
Our aim is to provide support that is purposeful, coordinated and responsive, while helping pupils build independence wherever possible.
Working with Specialist Professionals
Where additional expertise is needed, we may seek advice from external professionals and services.
These may include Educational Psychologists, specialist teachers, Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists and other relevant services.
The involvement of external professionals depends on individual needs, referral criteria and service availability.
We value the contribution of families and pupils throughout this process and aim to ensure that specialist recommendations inform practical support within the academy.
Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs)
Some children and young people with more significant or complex special educational needs may require an Education, Health and Care needs assessment.
An Education, Health and Care Plan is a statutory document that identifies a child or young person’s needs, intended outcomes and the special educational provision required to support them.
An EHCP is not required to access our Targeted Plus Offer. Support is considered in response to identified needs, and a formal diagnosis or EHCP does not automatically determine which internal interventions or arrangements will be appropriate.
Where a pupil has an EHCP, we work with families and relevant professionals to deliver and review the provision specified in their plan.
Further information about identifying needs, requesting support and the EHCP process can be found on our Supporting Your Child page.
Maintaining Connection with Mainstream Learning
Our aim is for pupils to remain connected to their learning, peers and wider academy community.
Where personalised arrangements are needed, we seek to ensure that these support participation, build confidence and develop independence.
Additional provision is carefully considered and reviewed, with a focus on helping pupils access their education as successfully and fully as possible.
Explore Our Inclusion and SEND Offer
Our Universal Offer — Inclusive teaching and everyday adjustments that support all pupils.
Our Targeted Offer — Additional planned interventions and support for identified needs.
Supporting Your Child — Information about identifying needs, reviewing support and working with families.
The Harbour — Learn about our internal inclusion centre and how it supports pupils as part of the academy’s wider provision.
Personalised support. Shared understanding. High aspirations for every pupil.

Supporting your child
Supporting Your Child
At Atlantic Academy, we recognise that every child and young person is different. Some pupils may experience difficulties with learning, communication, emotional wellbeing or participation in school at different points in their education.
We believe that identifying needs early, listening to families and working together are essential to providing effective support.
Whether your child needs an adjustment to everyday classroom practice or more individualised provision, our aim is to help them feel confident, included and successful.
I’m Concerned About My Child. What Should I Do?
If you have concerns about your child’s learning, development, communication, wellbeing or experience of school, we encourage you to get in touch.
You do not need to wait for a formal diagnosis or assessment before discussing your concerns with us.
Your child’s class teacher or tutor is a helpful starting point. They can discuss how your child is getting on, share observations and consider whether any additional strategies or support may be helpful.
Where further support is needed, staff can involve our Inclusion Team to help identify barriers to learning and consider appropriate provision.
We value the knowledge that parents and carers bring. Sharing what works well at home, any difficulties your child experiences and their own views can help us develop a fuller understanding of their needs.
Meet Our Inclusion Team
Our Inclusion Team works alongside teachers, pastoral staff, pupils and families to identify additional needs, coordinate support and help every child thrive.
The team helps to ensure that support is appropriate, consistent and responsive as pupils’ needs develop.
Miss Ramsey (Primary SENDCo)
Mrs Delage-Townsend (Secondary SENDCo)
Mr Andrew Clark (Assistant Principal, Inclusion)
Contact Our Inclusion Team
How Do We Identify Additional Needs?
We recognise that pupils’ strengths, needs and circumstances can change over time.
Teachers, pastoral staff and the Inclusion Team work together to identify potential barriers to learning and participation.
Identifying a difficulty does not automatically mean that a pupil has special educational needs or requires specialist intervention.
Our priority is to understand the barriers they are experiencing and identify the most appropriate support.
Reviewing progress, attainment and classroom assessments.
Listening to the pupil’s experiences and views.
Considering information or recommendations from other professionals.
Our Graduated Approach: Assess, Plan, Do, Review
When a pupil requires additional support, we use a graduated approach known as Assess, Plan, Do, Review.
This is an ongoing process that helps us understand individual needs, put appropriate strategies in place and evaluate their impact.
1. Assess — Understanding the Need
We gather information about the pupil’s strengths, difficulties and experiences.
This may include teacher assessments, observations, screening tools and discussions with the pupil and their family.
Our aim is to develop a clear understanding of what may be preventing the pupil from making progress or participating fully in school life.
2. Plan — Agreeing the Support
We identify the strategies, adjustments or interventions that may help.
We consider what we want the support to achieve, who will be involved and when progress will be reviewed.
The views of the pupil and their family help inform this planning.
3. Do — Putting Support into Practice
Staff implement the agreed strategies and interventions.
High-quality classroom teaching remains central to the pupil’s education, with additional support provided where appropriate.
Teachers, support staff and the Inclusion Team work together to promote a consistent approach.
4. Review — Evaluating the Impact
We consider how well the support is working.
This includes reviewing progress, listening to the pupil and their family, and evaluating whether the intended outcomes are being achieved.
Support may then continue, change, increase or reduce depending on the pupil’s needs.
Assess, Plan, Do, Review is a continuing cycle, not a one-off process. As pupils develop and their circumstances change, we adapt our approach accordingly.
Individual Learning Plans
Where a pupil has identified additional needs or barriers to learning, we may create an individual Learning Plan.
A Learning Plan helps teachers and other relevant staff understand:
For many pupils, a Learning Plan will primarily identify strategies from our Universal Offer, such as clear instructions, additional processing time, visual resources or adapted classroom activities.
Other pupils may benefit from additional Targeted or Targeted Plus support.
Learning Plans are shared with relevant staff to promote consistency across the academy. They are reviewed and updated as needs develop, taking account of the views of pupils, families and staff.
Having a Learning Plan does not automatically mean that a pupil requires specialist intervention or support outside the classroom.
The pupil’s strengths and areas of difficulty.
Working with External Professionals
Sometimes, additional specialist advice can help us better understand a pupil’s needs and identify appropriate support.
Where necessary, we may work with or seek advice from professionals such as:
Specialist involvement is considered according to individual needs. Access to external services may depend on referral criteria and availability.
Where professional advice is received, we consider how recommendations can inform the support provided in school.
Explore Dorset Council’s SEND Local Offer
If you would like advice and support on SEND from an impartial service, please get in touch with Dorset Sendias (SEN and Disability Information, Advice and Support Service).
Educational Psychologists.
Specialist teachers.
Speech and Language Therapists.
Occupational Therapists.
Other relevant health, education or support services.
Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs)
Some children and young people with more significant or complex special educational needs may require an Education, Health and Care needs assessment.
An Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) is a statutory document that identifies a child or young person’s needs, intended outcomes and the special educational provision required to support them.
An EHCP is not required for a pupil to receive additional support through our Targeted or Targeted Plus Offers.
Where a pupil has an EHCP, we work with families and relevant professionals to deliver and review the provision specified in their plan.
If you would like to discuss whether an Education, Health and Care needs assessment may be appropriate for your child, please contact our Inclusion Team.
Working in Partnership
We recognise that parents and carers know their children well and have an important role in understanding their strengths, experiences and needs.
We aim to work openly and constructively with families, sharing information, listening to concerns and involving them in decisions about support.
We also believe that children and young people should have opportunities to express their own views and contribute to decisions about their education wherever appropriate.
By working together, we can help pupils develop the confidence, independence and skills they need to thrive.
Further Information
You can explore our wider inclusion provision through the following pages:

Our Universal Offer — Inclusive teaching and everyday adjustments for all pupils.
Our Targeted Offer — Additional planned support for identified needs.
Our Targeted Plus Offer — Highly personalised and coordinated support.

Contact Our Inclusion Team

pageCache.text:
The Harbour
The Harbour
At Atlantic Academy, we recognise that some pupils need additional support at particular points in their school experience.
The Harbour is an important part of our wider inclusion provision, offering a supportive environment for pupils who may need additional help with learning, emotional regulation, wellbeing or engagement in school.
Our aim is to help pupils feel safe, supported and understood, while developing the confidence, skills and independence they need to participate successfully in their education.
A Space Designed to Support Individual Needs
The Harbour provides a range of spaces that can be used to support different aspects of a pupil’s development and wellbeing.
These include areas for learning, emotional regulation, sensory support and individual or small-group work.
We recognise that pupils may need different types of support at different times. For some, this might involve a short period of support to manage emotions or prepare to return to learning. For others, it may involve more structured, planned support over a longer period.
The Harbour enables staff to respond to identified needs within a supportive and purposeful environment.
How Does The Harbour Support Pupils?
Support within The Harbour is tailored to individual needs and may include:
The support provided will depend upon the pupil’s identified needs and the intended outcomes of their individual support arrangements.
A Place of Support, Not a Destination
The Harbour is part of Atlantic Academy’s inclusive approach to education.
It is not intended to replace a pupil’s wider school experience. Instead, it provides additional support that helps pupils remain connected to their learning, their peers and the wider academy community.
Our focus is on helping pupils develop the strategies, confidence and independence needed to participate as fully as possible in mainstream lessons and school life.
For some pupils, support may be brief and focused on a particular difficulty. Others may benefit from more structured arrangements that are regularly reviewed.
Our ambition remains the same: to help every pupil experience success, belonging and positive engagement with their education.
How Is Support Through The Harbour Arranged?
Access to The Harbour is based on identified individual needs and is planned and reviewed by appropriate academy staff.
The Harbour forms part of our wider Inclusion and SEND Offer, which includes Universal, Targeted and Targeted Plus support.
Where provision through The Harbour is appropriate, staff consider the pupil’s needs, the purpose of the support and how it will contribute to their learning, wellbeing and participation in school.
Support is reviewed to ensure that it remains purposeful and responsive as pupils’ needs develop.
Working Together
We recognise the importance of working in partnership with pupils and their families.
If you have concerns about your child’s learning, wellbeing or engagement in school, we encourage you to contact the academy so that we can discuss their needs and consider appropriate support.
You can find further information about how we identify additional needs, plan provision and review progress on our Supporting Your Child page.
You may also wish to explore:

pageCache.text:
Our House System: A Belonging Model
Three Houses. One Atlantic. Everyone belongs.
From Reception to Year 11, every student and member of staff belongs to one of our three Houses. Each House provides a smaller community within Atlantic where students are known, valued and encouraged to participate, lead and contribute.
Our House system brings Atlantic’s vision to life. It nurtures self-worth by giving every student a strong sense of identity and belonging. It inspires engagement through shared experiences, challenges and celebrations. It develops purpose by creating opportunities for students to lead, serve others and make a positive difference.
I am known, valued and proud to belong.
I participate, collaborate and embrace opportunities.
I contribute, lead and make a difference.
Meet our Houses
Castle Cove
Finding our voice, understanding our story and creating a legacy of which we can be proud.
Explore Castle Cove →
Chesil Cove
Exploring our world with curiosity, asking thoughtful questions and caring for the environment around us.
Explore Chesil Cove →
Church Ope Cove
Innovation and Performance
Developing creativity, expressing our ideas and having the confidence to turn possibilities into action.
Explore Church Ope Cove →
Belonging at Atlantic
Atlantic is one Academy, but our Houses create smaller communities in which relationships can grow. Students remain part of their House throughout their all-through journey, building connections across year groups and developing a lasting sense of identity and pride.
House Life in action
House life creates opportunities for students of all ages to participate together, represent their community and discover new strengths.
Every contribution strengthens our community.
Whether students lead an event, support a teammate, represent their House, improve their attendance or show kindness to someone else, they help make Atlantic a place where everyone belongs.

Attendance Matters
Attendance is very important to us and as a school we aim for 95% attendance for every pupil.
There are very few circumstances under which any term time absence may be authorised by law. Any absence for holidays in term time will be unauthorised and may be subject to a fine.
The government have changed their threshold for ‘persistent absenteeism’ to 90%.

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding, eSafety and Student Welfare - Atlantic Academy
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding, eSafety and Student Welfare
The Academy takes the welfare and safety of students very seriously, working hard to reduce all the kinds of harm that children can suffer, including abuse, bullying, discrimination and avoidable injuries. We strive to make sure that every student in the Academy feels secure, well cared for, and able to reach their full potential.
The Academy understands and is committed to the vital contribution that all governors, staff, parents and students can make to safeguarding children. All our staff are regularly and thoroughly trained in identifying, dealing with and reporting any safeguarding concerns.
Working together
We will continue to ensure that all our staff, parents or carers and students work together to know the rules about keeping children safe. They will understand the importance of following procedures and listening to each other, especially when there are concerns about safety.
Email contacts are available below but if you have any concerns at all about the safety or welfare of a child, please make immediate contact by telephone on 01305 820262 and be sure to make it clear that there may be a safeguarding issue. If you believe that a child is in imminent danger, please contact the police by dialling 999.
The Academy Lead Designated Child Protection Officer is Miss Heppell and Mrs Greaves, who can be contacted by clicking here.
Student welfare
The Academy has a range of policies and procedures in place that ensure the welfare of all of our students.
Several of these policies set out expectations about behaviour. This includes good learning behaviour around the Academy and in lessons as well as rules about how to communicate and behave appropriately towards other students and staff. This ensures everyone feels safe and can learn.
If you have any questions or concerns regarding the welfare of your son or daughter, we suggest that you contact your child’s pastoral lead in the first instance, they can be contacted here. If you would like to talk to another member of the staff, please contact atlanticoffice@atlantic-aspirations.org, or use the contact us form which can be found here.
